exposure: Women undergoing their first cesarean section under elective conditions were grouped by single (n = 295) or a parallel layer (n = 202) uterine closure technique.
cohort: Women undergoing their first cesarean section under elective conditions (n = 497).
finding: The parallel-layer closure, compared to a single-layer closure of the uterine incision in patients undergoing primary cesarean section, decreased the incidence of isthmocele formation and increased residual myometrial thickness.
mod_finding: The parallel-layer closure technique, compared to a single-layer closure, during cesarean section decreased the incidence of isthmocele formation and increased residual myometrial thickness.
